head_commit.message:
ci: check vendored kernel fixtures against the kernel at the pinned commit

Add a kernel-vectors job that downloads conformance/vector-lock.json
from actenon-kernel at fixtures/KERNEL_PIN, checks every vendored locked
fixture's sha256 against it (and the vendored lock copy for byte
identity), and compares each fixtures/KERNEL_UNLOCKED file, which the
kernel's lock does not cover, byte-for-byte with the kernel tree at the
pin. A pin that does not resolve fails the download.

head_commit.message:
fix: add .gitignore + --allow-dirty to publish workflow

The publish workflow failed because cargo test creates a target/
directory that shows as uncommitted changes. Fixes:
- Added .gitignore (/target, *.rs.bk, *.crate) so target/ is not tracked.
- Added --allow-dirty to both cargo publish --dry-run and cargo publish
  so the publish proceeds even if target/ exists from the test step.
- Removed the tag-only condition on the publish step so workflow_dispatch
  also publishes (needed for manual triggers).

head_commit.message:
fix: bundle conformance fixtures so tests run standalone

The tests referenced fixtures via relative paths to the parent
actenon-kernel repo (../../conformance/vectors/...). Now that the Rust
SDK is in its own repo, those paths don't resolve.

Fix: copied all needed conformance vector fixtures into a local
fixtures/ directory and updated the test paths to point there.

Verified: cargo test --all passes (19 tests: 8 verifier + 5
countersignature + 4 transparency + 1 trust_artifacts + 1
conformance). cargo publish --dry-run succeeds (57 files, 195.2KiB).

To publish to crates.io, a maintainer needs to:
1. Create a crates.io account (sign in with GitHub at crates.io)
2. Generate an API token at https://crates.io/settings/tokens
   (scope: publish-new + publish-update)
3. Add it as a GitHub secret named CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN in
   Actenon/sdk-rust → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
4. Push a new tag (e.g. v0.1.1) — the publish.yml workflow will
   publish automatically.

head_commit.message:
Initial Rust verifier SDK — v0.1.0

Minimal protected-endpoint verifier SDK for Rust, aligned to the Python
kernel's public action_intent and pccb contracts.

Mirrors the Rust SDK from actenon-kernel/sdk/rust/ into its own
repository so Rust users can use it as a git dependency:
  cargo add --git https://github.com/Actenon/sdk-rust

crates.io publication is prepared (Cargo.toml has all required fields;
publish workflow is included) but pending the CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
secret. Once the token is added, pushing a v* tag will publish
automatically.

Scope:
- action_intent v1 and pccb v1 Rust data structures
- protected-endpoint proof verification
- exact audience, tenant, subject, action, target, action-hash,
  not-before, and expiry checks
- optional verifier-side clock skew tolerance (default zero)
- deterministic local-proof verification (HS256)
- custom signature verification via SignatureVerifier trait
- offline Receipt counter-signature verification
- offline, fail-closed issuer-status verification
- signed exact-action approval verification
